Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a reported fall onto an outstretched hand. The
mechanism described is consistent with the distal radius injury identified on examination and imaging, and the
findings clearly confirm a fracture in that location. Initial management included immobilization in a splint, analgesia,
and orthopedic follow-up. Over three visits the patient's pain and swelling steadily decreased, range of motion
improved, and the plan was tapered from immobilization to a home exercise program as healing progressed. The
patient also mentioned a minor wrist strain several years ago that resolved completely without lasting limitation.
Treatment has been appropriate to the injury and the course has followed the expected pattern. Billed services reflect
the visits documented here, with no duplicate charges identified.
